comment: Known differences between two canonical graph dumps (jets/rulesbench/graphdump), read by rules_bench_diff and embedded in it. A difference is unclassified unless an entry matches. Fields and pair kinds: README.md beside this file. Each entry names where the difference is recorded: a section of jets/jetrules/rete/README.md or a register entry of projects/rules_benchmark.

entries.description: The line is the same on both sides up to the label of a minted node, under a one-to-one correspondence of labels: the node is on both sides and was renamed because its neighbourhood within three hops differs. What differs is in its own lines, which are classified on their own.

refs: jets/jetrules/rete/README.md, The Go and C++ engines are independently maintained and they disagree, item 3
entries.description: The Go engine quantises a double literal to 15 bits of mantissa (ResourceManager.NewDoubleLiteral); C++ keeps it. The two values are equal once both are quantised.

The Go engine names a lookup result jets:lookup:<key> (jets:lookup:multi:<key> for a multi-lookup), without the table, so two tables looked up with the same key share one subject, which carries both tables' columns and both rows' jets:row_id (LookupTableSqlite3.Lookup, jets/jetrules/rete/lookup_table_sqlite3.go). C++ names it jets:<table>:<key> (LookupTable::lookup_internal, jets/rete/lookup_sql_helper.cc), one subject per table. In the dump: one minted node on Go where C++ has one per table. Only a lookup subject: the merged node must be the object of a cache triple (jets:cache:<table> jets:lookup_row|jets:lookup_multi_rows _:node) on Go; any other node merged on one engine stays unclassified.
entries.subject: jets:cache:.*

entries.description: A multi-lookup's cache triple: Go writes (jets:cache:<table> jets:lookup_multi_rows <subject>) (LookupTableSqlite3.MultiLookup), C++ (<table> jets:lookup_row <subject>) (LookupTable::lookup_internal), which the dump renames jets:cache:<table>. Bookkeeping: the 26 uses of jets:lookup_row and jets:lookup_multi_rows in the four workspaces' rule files (counted 2026-10-20) all read them as (?x jets:lookup_… ?y), and none names a cache resource.
entries.subject: jets:cache:.*

refs: jets/jetrules/rete/README.md, The Go and C++ engines are independently maintained and they disagree, item 3
entries.description: A ratio the Go engine computed from quantised literals: at most 2.5 quanta of Go's 15-bit grid from the C++ value, a quantum being graphdump.Quantum at the larger magnitude (on cm_loop the largest is 2.10 quanta). Limited to the percentages, hc_usi:medicarePct, _0:medicarePct and their export usi_out:PercentMedTagGlobal. A money amount computed from quantised literals is not classified, since it changes by cents (on cm_loop: hc_usi:medicareGlobal, totalAmountAllowed, totalAmountPaid, mbrResponsibility and the export's Amt* columns, 0.5 to 1.04 quanta apart). Weaker evidence than go-double-literal-quantised, and reported apart from it.

Text + double writes the number differently: Go formats it with %v, the shortest form (Node.ADD, jets/jetrules/rdf/ast_math_operators.go), and C++ with std::to_string, six decimals (AddVisitor, jets/rete/expr_op_arithmetics.h). "rate: 991" on Go is "rate: 991.000000" on C++ (usi_ws gz02, 4_CM04_Orphans_Main1.jr). Matched only on hc_usi:meetRule, and only when the texts are equal between their numbers and each differing pair of numbers is one six-decimal form against one other form, equal once quantised; integers that differ are not matched.

refs: jets/jetrules/rete/README.md, Operator names are not registered anywhere but the two factories (apply_regex)
entries.description: literal_regex returns the whole match, or an empty string on no match, on Go (ApplyRegexOp.Eval), and capture group 1, or null on no match, on C++ (RegexVisitor). usi_ws z004 (^(\d\d\d) on a rendering provider zip): a zip that does not start with three digits gives an empty hc_usi:claimZip3 on Go and none on C++.

literal_regex as in literal-regex-claimZip3, on walrus_ws's name-splitting rules (merge_claim_header_and_details_main.jr): Go's pt_fname keeps the comma and the space (", John") and its pt_lname the comma ("Doe,"), and C++'s are the capture groups ("John", "Doe"). Matched as a pair: Go's text has that form and contains C++'s.
